updates.text: Released GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst and GPT-Image-2.6 Flare for image generation and editing, with adjustable complexity, SVG generation, and animated GIF generation. Added markup-guided editing for supported GPT Image 2.5 and 2.6 models.

Added automatic review for eligible Agents API projects. Set the session's review field to "auto_review" to have a model approve or deny supported tool and permission requests based on conversation intent and risk. See the automatic review guide for supported requests, limitations, and additional to
Released GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast, efficient model for visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clear, natural writing.
Added Ultrafast mode to the Agents API. Set agent.service_tier to ultrafast with a supported model to reduce the time between generated tokens.

Added native Decisions integration in GPT-Live. Your app can act while your user is speaking or react to what Live says. Let Live call Decisions directly through native delegation, or trigger decisions as input or output transcript deltas arrive.

You can now pre-warm an OpenAI-hosted sandbox before attaching it to an Agents API session. Prewarming improves latency by creating and configuring the sandbox before a user finishes sending their message. This means the user doesn't have to wait for all this work to complete.

Added Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol in the Responses API. Use gpt-6.1-sol with service_tier: "ultrafast" to reduce the time between generated output tokens. It is available to all API users, subject to rate limits, with global processing and US and EU data residency. See Ultrafast pricing.

Updated the chat-latest snapshot, which points to the latest model available in ChatGPT for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users. Released the Decisions API in beta with gpt-6-luna. Turn text and images into typed answers 10x faster than the Responses API.

Simplified API usage tiers from five to three: Build, Launch, and Grow. Organizations automatically upgrade as total credit purchases reach tier minimums. See usage tiers for monthly usage limits and how to view rate limits for each model.
​Analytics API: credit-usage response update
low (low@2026-10-24.0): max output tokens rise from 32,768 to 128,000. web_search max_tokens and max_tokens_per_page rise from 2,000 to 4,000. fetch_url content extraction uses openai/gpt-6-luna.
medium (medium@2026-10-22.1): web_search max_tokens and max_tokens_per_page rise from 2,000 to 4,000. fetch_url content extraction uses openai/gpt-6-luna.

high (high@2026-10-28.0): uses openai/gpt-6.1-terra instead of openai/gpt-6-sol. Max steps rise from 15 to 40, and a run makes at most 40 tool calls. web_search max_tokens and max_tokens_per_page rise from 2,000 to 4,000. fetch_url content extraction uses openai/gpt-6-luna.

xhigh (xhigh@2026-10-29.0): stays on anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, with openai/gpt-6.1-sol as the fallback model. Max steps rise from 100 to 300, and context compaction starts at 150,000 tokens. xhigh sets no system prompt, so its frozen configuration no longer sends instructions.
Step budget reminders: low, medium, high, and xhigh remind the model of its remaining step budget as it works. fast runs one step and has no reminders.
Automatic health-based routing and failover across model deployments
Per-token pricing at each model’s published rates, with no per-request fees
Claude Sonnet 5 — anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, Anthropic’s latest Sonnet model.
Kimi K2.7 Code — perplexity/kimi-k2.7-code, Moonshot AI’s coding and agentic model.

This page lists the latest features and improvements for Microsoft 365 Copilot. It includes changes that are generally available (Current Channel for Microsoft 365 apps) and specific to each platform.
Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.
Navigate to your workbook changes directly from the Copilot chat pane response [Windows, Web, Mac]
In Copilot in Excel, the response contains links to highlight where changes are made in your workbook. Navigate directly to new sheets, tables, ranges, and objects like charts and shapes.

What changed: In the Copilot chat response, there now is a link you can click that will take you directly to changes in the workbook. Previously, you would need to locate the change in the response and navigate in the sheet on your own.

Why: We want you to understand where copilot made edits and connect you to them directly from the chat response. This will help build confidence in the changes and allow you to review while you're reading the response in the chat pane.
Send a prompt to Copilot where the workbook is modified.
The chat response will show the changes in a different format with a highlight to indicate a link you can click for navigation. New Sheets, tables, ranges, and objects will be highlighted.
Why this matters: The feature allows quick review of document changes made by Copilot, increasing transparency of the edits.
Business impact: Teams can understand changes made while reading the response from Copilot and quickly navigate to those places for review.
